# GitHub Wiki

## Detect

- The user names a wiki or gives `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/wiki`. A wiki is a separate git repository; nothing in the main repo signals it.
- In a clone: the remote ends in `.wiki.git`; `Home.<ext>` at the root; optional `_Sidebar.<ext>` and `_Footer.<ext>`; files named like page titles; `[[...]]` links; no config file.
- Not a wiki: Docsify, which uses a lowercase `_sidebar.md` beside an `index.html` that sets `window.$docsify`. Check real filename case with `git ls-files`.

## Get the source

### From the repo

- `git clone https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>.wiki.git`. Only the default branch is published.
- Every file in a markup format GitHub renders is a page (https://github.com/github/markup#markups). Convert non-Markdown pages to Markdown first (for example `pandoc -t gfm`).

### From an export

None; use the `.wiki.git` clone.

### From the live site

GitHub's own page list: `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/wiki/_pages`. Use the clone for sources.

Reference: https://docs.github.com/en/communities/documenting-your-project-with-wikis

## Config → docs.json

Wikis have no config.

| Wiki source                                               | docs.json                         |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| repository name / About description                       | `name` / `description`            |
| repository URL                                            | `navbar.links` (`type: github`)   |
| image at the top of `_Sidebar.md`                         | `logo`                            |
| external links in `_Sidebar.md`                           | `navigation.global.anchors`       |
| `_Footer.md` links                                        | `footer.links` / `footer.socials` |
| `_Footer.md` prose, revision info, wiki search, clone box | drop and report                   |

## Navigation

- `_Sidebar.md` is free-form Markdown. A heading, bold line or unlinked list item with children → group; nested lists → nested groups; a heading that links a page → group with that page as `root`; each page link → a page, in order.
- Sidebar links to headings (`Page#section`) have no sidebar slot: report.
- A page listed twice keeps its first position. `[[Home]]` is the home page.
- Pages missing from `_Sidebar.md` were still reachable from GitHub's page list: ask the user where they go.
- No `_Sidebar.md`: GitHub showed only the alphabetical page list.
- A `_Sidebar.md` inside a folder applies to that folder's pages, often a translation: report it.

## Content conversion

- Flat namespace: a page's name is its file name without extension; folders do not count. Names match case-insensitively and treat `-` and space as the same. Build a page name → new path index (`Home` → the index page; `mint migrate --topic conversion`, Links); resolve name clashes by hand.
- The page title is the file name with `-` shown as a space. GitHub renders it above the body, so a body `# H1` is a section heading: drop it only if it repeats the page name.

| Wiki                                                                                                   | Mintlify                                                         |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `[[Page Name]]`                                                                                        | `[Page Name](/<path>)` via the table                             |
| `[[Link text\|Page Name]]` (text first in Markdown pages; Gollum order)                                | `[Link text](/<path>)`                                           |
| `[[Page Name#anchor]]`                                                                                 | `/<path>#anchor`                                                 |
| `[[text\|https://...]]`                                                                                | `[text](https://...)`                                            |
| `[[image.png]]`, `[[/path/image.png\|alt=Text]]`                                                       | `![Text](/path/image.png)`; other image options drop             |
| `[[Page\|Text]]` in `.mediawiki` pages                                                                 | MediaWiki order: page first                                      |
| `[[...]]` to a page that does not exist                                                                | plain text; report                                               |
| `[[_TOC_]]`                                                                                            | delete                                                           |
| `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/wiki/Page-Name`, `/<owner>/<repo>/wiki/Page-Name`, bare `Page-Name` | `/<path>` via the table                                          |
| relative links that leave the wiki (`../issues/12`, `../blob/main/x`)                                  | absolute GitHub URLs resolved from `/<owner>/<repo>/wiki/<page>` |
| `#user-content-x`                                                                                      | `#x`                                                             |
| `> [!NOTE]` style alerts                                                                               | (`mint migrate --topic conversion`, GitHub alerts)               |
| `:emoji:` shortcodes                                                                                   | the emoji                                                        |

Skip `[[...]]` inside code. Link syntax: https://github.com/gollum/gollum/wiki#link-tag

## Assets

- Non-page files in the wiki repo are served under the wiki URL. Copy every referenced file into the docs repo.
- Images hosted on `user-images.githubusercontent.com`, `github.com/user-attachments/...` or the main repo's `blob/` URLs: download them.

## URLs and redirects

- Old URLs are `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/wiki` (Home) and `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/wiki/<Page-Name>`. They stay on github.com and cannot redirect. Add no `redirects` for them, and do not tell the user they will redirect.
- Produce a route table instead (outside the docs content), one row per wiki page: `wiki_url`, `page_name`, `new_path`, `status` (`migrated`, `merged into <path>`, `dropped`).
- Offer, but do not do without approval: replace each wiki page with a "Moved to <new URL>" line, point `Home` and `_Sidebar.md` at the new site, then disable the wiki.

## Known gaps

- Old wiki URLs cannot redirect.
- Wiki revision history (kept only if the wiki is merged with `git subtree add`).
- Formatting lost when converting non-Markdown pages.
- `[[...]]` image options other than `alt`.
- Sidebar prose, images and heading links.
- Links that were already broken on the wiki, and links to `_pages`, `_history` or revision URLs.
- Heading anchors (`mint migrate --topic conversion`, Heading IDs).
